resources.string: PairFree는 블루투스로 이어폰을 제어하므로 접근 권한이 필요합니다. 나중에 상태 알림을 위해 알림 표시 및 이어폰과 앱 연결 권한을 요청할 수 있으며, 두 권한 모두 선택 사항입니다.
블루투스 접근 권한이 없으면 이어폰을 제어할 수 없습니다.
이어폰을 선택하세요. 제어 연결은 한 앱만 사용할 수 있으므로 공식 앱(PeatsAudio, Soundcore 등)을 먼저 종료하세요.
지원하는 이어폰이 페어링되어 있지 않습니다. 먼저 블루투스 설정에서 이어폰을 페어링하세요.
계정도, 인터넷 연결도 필요하지 않습니다. 모든 데이터는 휴대전화에만 남습니다.
%1$s의 제어 기능에 연결할 수 없습니다. %2$s 앱이 실행 중이면 종료하고, 이어폰이 오디오용으로 연결되었는지 확인한 뒤 다시 시도하세요.
%1$s의 제어 기능에 연결할 수 없습니다. 오디오 연결 상태를 확인하고(이어폰 착용 또는 케이스 열기) 다시 시도하세요.
PairFree의 블루투스 접근 권한이 꺼져 있습니다.
이 휴대전화에서 %1$s을(를) 설정하려면 Android 17이 필요합니다. Android 17 이전에는 Android 16 QPR3를 설치한 Pixel 또는 Android 16을 설치한 OnePlus, OPPO, realme 기기에서만 해당 블루투스 채널이 열립니다.
현재 Android 버전은 PairFree가 요청해도 %1$s 설정에 필요한 블루투스 소켓을 앱에 공개하지 않습니다. 루팅 없이 연결을 시도했습니다. 연결 진단 정보를 보내주시면 이 휴대전화의 동작을 확인하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
블루투스에서 주변의 %1$s을(를) 찾지 못했습니다. 이어폰을 케이스에서 꺼내 오디오 연결을 확인하고, 공식 앱을 종료한 뒤 다시 시도하세요.
%1$s에 연결하려면 주변 블루투스 기기를 검색할 권한이 필요합니다. PairFree는 이 권한을 위치 확인에 사용하지 않습니다.
오디오 코덱은 휴대전화에서 선택합니다. 삼성 휴대전화에서는 블루투스 설정에서도 이 이어폰의 LDAC가 켜져 있는지 확인하세요.
이어폰에서 LDAC를 사용할 수 있게 되었지만 실제 코덱은 휴대전화에서 선택합니다. 삼성 휴대전화는 블루투스 설정에서 이어폰 옆 톱니바퀴를 눌러 LDAC를 켜세요. 다른 기기에서는 고음질 오디오 같은 이름일 수 있습니다. Android 제한으로 PairFree는 휴대전화가 실제로 사용하는 코덱을 확인할 수 없습니다.
이 이어폰에서는 LDAC와 두 기기 연결을 동시에 사용할 수 없습니다. 한쪽을 켜면 다른 쪽이 꺼지며, 변경할 때마다 이어폰이 다시 연결되어 몇 초 걸립니다.
이 모델의 이퀄라이저는 아직 확인되지 않았습니다. 아래 버튼으로 Soundcore 앱의 EQ 설정 통신 기록을 보내주시면 지원에 도움이 됩니다.
아직 이 이어폰의 정보를 읽을 수 없습니다
Soundcore 앱에는 이 모델이 있지만 PairFree는 배터리 및 설정 정보를 읽는 방법을 아직 모릅니다. 기기 탭에서 진단 정보를 복사해 보내주세요. 이어폰의 응답 내용이 담겨 있어 모델 지원에 도움이 됩니다.
이 모델에서는 아직 시험하지 않았습니다. PairFree는 OpenSCQ30 코드에 따라 EQ를 전송합니다. 소리가 표시대로 바뀌지 않는다면 공식 앱의 설정 통신 기록을 보내주세요.
이 이어폰의 이퀄라이저는 아직 지원하지 않습니다. 아래 버튼을 눌러 공식 PeatsAudio 앱의 설정 통신 기록을 제공하면 기능 추가에 도움이 됩니다. 몇 분이면 됩니다.
이어폰이 현재 EQ를 알려주지 않고, 이 휴대전화에서 설정한 기록도 없습니다. 프로필을 선택하거나 주파수 대역을 조정하여 적용하세요.
프리셋의 음향 곡선은 고정되어 있습니다. 대역을 직접 조절하려면 새 프로필이나 저장한 프로필을 선택하세요.
프리셋의 음향 곡선은 고정되어 있습니다. 대역을 직접 조절하려면 기본 음향, 새 프로필 또는 저장한 프로필을 선택하세요.
이퀄라이저 곡선입니다. 아래 주파수 대역을 선택하여 조절하세요.
이 이어폰용 PairFree 프로필 파일이 아닙니다.
이 휴대전화에서 프로필이 삭제됩니다. 이어폰에는 현재 적용된 소리가 유지됩니다.
이어폰이 현재 EQ를 알려주므로 어떤 앱으로 설정했든 실제 적용된 상태가 표시됩니다.
이어폰은 프리셋 종류만 알려주며 사용자 지정 곡선은 알려주지 않습니다. 전원이 꺼지면 사용자 지정 곡선도 사라집니다. PairFree는 마지막으로 적용한 곡선을 저장했다가 연결할 때 다시 전송합니다.
이 프리셋은 이어폰이 직접 적용합니다. 삼성은 음향 곡선 정보를 공개하지 않습니다.
모든 대역의 0 dB는 이어폰의 기본 음향입니다. 이어폰이 현재 EQ를 알려주지 않으므로 PairFree는 공식 앱처럼 연결할 때마다 이 휴대전화에서 마지막으로 사용한 설정을 다시 적용합니다.
양쪽 이어폰을 모두 착용했을 때 적용되는 동작입니다. 한쪽만 사용할 때의 동작은 별도로 저장되며, 한쪽만 착용하면 이곳에 표시됩니다.
한쪽만 착용 중이므로 한쪽 이어폰 사용 시의 동작이 표시됩니다. 양쪽을 모두 착용하면 양쪽 사용 시 동작이 표시됩니다.
끄면 이어폰이 터치와 길게 누르기를 무시합니다.
터치 입력이 인식될 때 이어폰에서 소리가 납니다.
모든 터치 및 길게 누르기 동작이 출고 당시 기본값으로 돌아갑니다.
이어폰에서 터치 제어 정보를 제공하지 않았습니다.
주변 환경에 맞춰 노이즈 캔슬링과 주변 소리 듣기를 자동으로 조합합니다.
적응형 오디오가 통과시키는 주변 소리의 양입니다. 0은 가장 많이, 100은 가장 적게 들립니다.
말을 시작하면 미디어 음량을 낮추고 주변 목소리를 들려줍니다.
주변 환경에 따라 미디어 음량을 조절합니다.
Turn the Digital Crown the other way
Lets pressing and holding the stem switch noise control off too.
Turns the music down and lets voices through, for a quick talk.
Lets in a little ambient sound, so the ears do not feel blocked while noise cancelling is off.
Makes voices stand out in ambient sound.
Adds one more ambient sound level.
Allows noise cancelling and ambient sound with only one earbud in.
When you start talking, the earbuds switch to ambient sound and lower the media volume.
Double tap the edge for volume
Double tap the edge of the left earbud for volume down, of the right for volume up.
Hear your own voice more clearly on calls.
Calls play through the earbuds while they are in your ears, and through the phone when they are not.
Switch between your Samsung devices without pairing again.
Wake the voice assistant by voice
The earbuds beep loudly: take them out of your ears first. Mute one to hear the other.

Google\'s Find Hub rings and finds Pixel Buds. It uses a key the earbuds share with your Google account, which only Google Play services holds, so PairFree opens Find Hub, as the Pixel Buds app leaves it to Play services.
Take the earbuds out of your ears first. The beep is loud.

The earbuds play quiet tones at eight pitches, from low to high. Tap I hear it as soon as you hear one; when you hear nothing, wait. Find a quiet place and put both earbuds in. The test turns media volume up to the top and puts it back afterwards; the tones themselves stay quiet. It takes about three minutes, and gives an equalizer that lifts what you hear less, as SOUNDPEATS\' app works it out.
Stop the music or video playing first: it would play at full volume during the test.
Listen for the tone. A tone you do not hear ends on its own.
Done. Each pitch gets the gain for the quietest tone you heard.
No fit test of its own on these earbuds: PairFree can check the seal with low tones from the phone, one earbud at a time, as JBL\'s app does.

A low tone is only heard well when the ear tip seals your ear canal. PairFree plays a low tone in one earbud at a time, normal and then softer, and you say whether you hear it. Put both earbuds in, find a quiet place and stop any music or video first. The phone\'s media volume goes to the top for the check and back after.
A tone is playing in the %1$s earbud
A softer tone is playing in the %1$s earbud
Do you hear a low tone? Adjust the earbud if you do not, then answer.
For a fair or poor seal, adjust the earbud or try another ear tip size and run the check again. The levels are PairFree\'s own, so compare the two earbuds with each other.

The earbuds play a tone for each of twelve points, six pitches in each earbud. Move the slider to the quietest level at which you still hear the tone, then tap Next. Find a quiet place and put both earbuds in. At the end the earbuds work out your hearing enhancement and it is switched on.
Lower the slider until the tone fades away, then raise it a little.
Done. The earbuds have your hearing enhancement and it is on; the Sound tab\'s switch turns it off.

Play some music you know well. PairFree switches the earbuds between two sounds, A and B: tap A or B to hear each, then keep the one you like better. It then tries a small change to your favourite, up to twelve times, and ends with a curve to save. If you cannot tell them apart, keep A. Leaving early puts the earbuds back as they were.
Switch between A and B while the music plays.
Keep the one I am listening to
Done. The earbuds are playing the sound you preferred.
Go back to how it was

Adapt Sound: the earbuds play quiet tones, one earbud and one pitch at a time, and you say whether you hear each one. Find a quiet place, put both earbuds in and stop any music or video first. The result is kept on the earbuds as your Adapt Sound profile.
Do you hear it? If you cannot hear a tone, answer No.
Done. Each pitch has a level from 5 (quiet tones heard) to 40 (loud tones needed), left then right. Adapt Sound is on with this profile.
Check that each ear tip seals well. A good seal gives fuller bass and better noise cancelling.
Put both earbuds in your ears and stay still somewhere quiet. The earbuds play a short sound and check how well each ear tip seals. It takes about 10 seconds.
Noise control turns off for the test and back on afterwards.
For an earbud with a poor fit, push it in a little further and twist it slightly so the tip seals, then test again. If it still does not fit, try a larger ear tip.
No result came back. Check that both earbuds are connected and in your ears, then try again.
Plays a series of sounds for about 30 seconds to push water out of the speakers, for example after rain or a workout. Take the earbuds out of your ears first.
Draining. The earbuds stop by themselves after about 30 seconds.
Uses Bluetooth LE Audio where the phone supports it. The earbuds restart to switch and reconnect by themselves.

PairFree learns what a model can do, and its equalizer, from what its official app (PeatsAudio, Soundcore, Galaxy Wearable, Sound Connect or Nothing X) reads from the earbuds and sends to them. Android can log that, and one recording per model is enough to add it for everyone.
Turn on Developer options: in Settings, open About phone and tap Build number seven times. On Samsung it is under About phone, Software information.
In Settings, Developer options, set Bluetooth HCI snoop log to Enabled (not Filtered). Then turn Bluetooth off and on.

Open the official app for these earbuds with them connected. Open each of its screens once, so it reads every setting. Then change each setting you want PairFree to learn, one at a time and a few seconds apart, and note what you changed. Do not come back to PairFree yet. If PairFree\'s status notification shows for these earbuds, set it to None on the Device tab first: while it shows, the official app cannot connect.
On SOUNDPEATS earbuds, also run PeatsAudio\'s fit test if it has one, and on its EQ screen tap SOUNDPEATS Classic and every other preset once, a few seconds apart.
Back in Developer options, tap Take bug report, then Full report.
It takes several minutes, and Android shows nothing while it works. Wait for the notification that says it is ready.
When the notification says the bug report is ready, tap it and share it to PairFree. If you miss the notification, tap Choose a bug report below, open the menu and pick Bug reports to find it.

PairFree shows what it found. On SOUNDPEATS earbuds, name the EQ curves in the order you tapped them. Then send the report, and write in it what you changed in the official app. If PairFree is connected to the same earbuds, its own device report goes in too.

Afterwards, set Bluetooth HCI snoop log back to Disabled and delete the bug report. It holds a lot of personal data: send PairFree\'s report, never the bug report itself, since GitHub issues are public.
Reading the bug report. This can take a minute.

PairFree reads the bug report only on this phone. From the Bluetooth log inside it, it reads only the messages exchanged with earbuds of the brands PairFree supports, and skips everything else. Known messages have addresses and serial numbers masked. Unknown messages show only short previews and technical summaries. Soundcore transfers can include sizes, timing and recognized file-format details; filenames, identifiers, audio contents and known sleep-history messages are left out. It does not keep the file. Nothing is sent until you submit the report yourself in your browser. PairFree has no internet access at all.
This bug report has no Bluetooth log. Set Bluetooth HCI snoop log to Enabled, turn Bluetooth off and on, use the official app again, then take a new bug report.

The Bluetooth log in this bug report has nothing from earbuds PairFree supports. Check that the snoop log was set to Enabled, not Filtered, and Bluetooth turned off and on, before you used the official app.
That file is not a bug report.
All of them are presets PairFree already knows, named for you.
From %1$s, when you opened this recording.
Not in the log. Turning Bluetooth off and on before opening PeatsAudio records it. The report is still useful without it.
A model PairFree does not know yet (%1$s)
PairFree\'s own device report for these earbuds goes in too.
To add PairFree\'s own device report as well, connect these earbuds in PairFree before sending.
No EQ curves in this recording. The settings are still worth sending.
At its end the report has a place to write what you changed in the official app, in order. That tells which message is which setting.
Name at least one curve to send the report.

Nothing has left this phone yet. Send on GitHub copies the report and opens a new issue with it filled in, in your browser. It is sent only when you submit the issue there. If the issue is empty, paste the report into it.
Copied. If the new issue on GitHub is empty, paste the report into it, then submit it.
Pause when an earbud is taken out
Sony\'s single noise cancelling setting, made for wind. Only while noise cancelling is on.
Pauses the music and lets in ambient sound when you start speaking.
Sony\'s upscaling for compressed music. On means automatic.
The earbuds report the preset or curve they hold, whichever app set it. They apply their presets themselves, so no curve is drawn for those. Clear Bass is below.
These Sony earbuds have not listed an equalizer, or have not answered yet.
Bose\'s steps, as its own app counts them.
Audio for the best sound, Video for the least delay behind the picture.
How much of your own voice you hear on calls.
Keeps the volume at a level that is safe for your hearing.
Pauses the music while you talk, and plays it again once you have stopped for the time chosen.
Playback: tap to play or pause, double tap for the next track, triple for the last, hold for the voice assistant
Noise control: tap to change the noise mode, double tap for TalkThru, hold for the voice assistant
Voice assistant: hold to talk to your phone\'s voice assistant
Volume: tap for louder, double tap for quieter, hold for the voice assistant
Keeps the bass and treble full when you listen quietly.
Noise cancelling adjusts itself to the noise around you.
Adjusts the sound to how the earbuds sit in your ears.
What tapping and holding this earbud does.
Apple\'s Beats app has no equalizer for Beats, so PairFree has none to show.
PairFree reads no battery from this Beats; Android shows it in its Bluetooth settings where the Beats report it. Its settings are on the Device tab.
HeyMelody\'s equalizer presets and the custom equalizers the earbuds keep are on this tab, when the earbuds report them.
AirPods have an equalizer only on Apple\'s newest beta firmware. Where they report one, it is below.
The equalizer shows once the headphones or earbuds report theirs. On some JBL models it goes another way in JBL\'s app, which PairFree does not send yet.
Bose earbuds and headphones have a tone control rather than an equalizer of bands by frequency. Where the model has one, it is below.
PairFree shows the equalizer once the earbuds have said which model they are, for the models it knows.
PairFree shows the equalizer once the earbuds have reported theirs. The older QCY models on JieLi\'s chips keep their equalizer in a setting PairFree does not send yet.
Turns the touch controls off, so lying on an earbud does not pause the music.
Spatial audio turns bass boost and the equalizer presets off while it is on.
The earbuds tune their sound to how they sit in your ears.
Makes voices in videos and podcasts clearer.
Keeps loud and quiet parts closer in volume.
Turns sudden loud sounds around you down.
The earbuds remind you to stretch when you have kept your head down for a while.
Your phone picks the codec when the earbuds connect. Reconnect them for a change to take effect.
Bluetooth plays from your phone. Local plays the sounds held on the earbuds, which lasts longer on a charge.
The earbuds stop the audio after the time chosen.
Double press and hold the dial to lock or unlock it.
Answer calls, or mute during a call
The battery and buttons for noise control in the notification shade while these earbuds are connected. PairFree keeps their connection open meanwhile, so their official app cannot connect.
Google\'s Fast Pair notification shows their battery. PairFree shows none.
PairFree shows no notification for these earbuds.

Google shows its own battery notification for these earbuds too, and PairFree cannot hide it. To see only one, turn Google\'s off in Google Play services\' notification settings. That covers every Fast Pair device on this phone.
Android does not let PairFree show notifications yet.

To show it when the earbuds connect while PairFree is closed, Android asks once to link PairFree to these earbuds. Its prompt says a linked app can sync information such as a caller\'s name; PairFree uses the link only to start this notification.
Show it when the earbuds connect?

Android starts PairFree\'s notification when these earbuds connect, with PairFree closed, only once PairFree is linked to them. Android\'s prompt that follows says a linked app can sync information such as a caller\'s name. PairFree uses the link only to start this notification, and it still has no internet access.
The battery and noise control of the connected earbuds.
Noise control: %1$s. Tap for the next mode.
Copied. Paste it into a device report issue on the project page to help support these earbuds.
Copied. Paste it into a new issue on the project page, so we can see why the connection failed.
Every setting on the earbuds goes back to how it left the factory. They may also forget this phone; then pair them again in the Bluetooth settings.
Adapt noise cancelling to the surroundings
Sound quality lets the phone use LDAC; a stable connection drops out less in crowded places.
Low, mid and high, on the AirPods firmware that has it.
The Pixel Buds Pro, Pro 2 and 2a have an equalizer, which shows here once they have reported it. The Pixel Buds (2020) and A-Series have bass boost, below.
Adjusts noise cancelling to your surroundings.
Enhances bass and treble at lower volume levels.
Only while you wear both earbuds. If it turns on by mistake, tap an earbud once to go back to noise cancelling.
You are told when the recommended exposure limit is exceeded.
While charging, at low battery, after pairing and on errors.
When an earbud is placed in the case properly. Case sounds change when the earbuds go back in the case.
Respond to calls and notifications with head movements.
Tap to mute and unmute during calls
Turns noise control on by itself while Live Translate runs, which needs Google\'s Translate app.
Sets the volume to suit the noise around you.
When sharing, each earbud\'s volume can be set on its own after a chime, and alerts play on both. Needs in-ear detection.
Improves bass and treble at lower volume levels.
The volume drops for a moment when the earbuds hear one of these sounds. Experimental: they may miss some, or take a similar sound for one.
The earbuds restart after a change, which takes about 20 seconds. aptX Adaptive and Lossless need aptX on; on most models LDAC and aptX do not go together, and LDAC does not go with two devices.
Some models restart after a change.
The earbuds restart and reconnect, which takes a few seconds.
The earbuds turn off. Turn them on again with their button, or by putting them in the case and taking them out.
Answer or switch between two calls
This EarFun model has no equalizer in EarFun\'s app.
Keeps the sound below this level.
Taps do nothing while this is on.
This 1MORE model has no equalizer in 1MORE\'s product list.
Game mode lowers the delay of the sound; LDAC raises its quality where your phone supports it. Your phone still picks the codec when the earbuds connect.
Pause, and play again when put back in
Plays your voice from the microphone back to you, so you can hear yourself while you talk.
The earbuds turn off once, when the time is up.
Switch noise control or an equalizer setting from the home screen.
Tap to set up PairFree\'s widget
PairFree needs the Bluetooth permission first. Open PairFree to allow it.
No supported earbuds are paired with this phone.
Some choices appear after these earbuds have connected to PairFree once.
PairFree has nothing to put on a widget button for these earbuds.
A 1×1 widget shows the first button; wider widgets show more of the first row, and two rows show the second.
The widget shows the buttons of whichever of these earbuds is connected.
Tick the choices to step through, in the order you tick them. Pick at least two.
